newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SOCCER-RANGERS' CUP HOPES HIT BY THREE-GOAL BURST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RANGERS' CUP HOPES HIT BY THREE-GOAL BURST.

text.p: Sweden's Gothenburg fired three second-half goals past a bungling Glasgow Rangers defence on Wednesday to leave the Scottish champions facing an early exit from the European Cup.
Rangers lost 3-0 in their preliminary round first-leg match and now face a virtually impossible task at home in two weeks' time.
After a sleepy first half, with Rangers apparently looking for a draw, the Scots conceded two goals in three minutes.
Rangers goalkeeper Andy Goram was helpless against a 20-metre scorcher from Stefan Pettersson, and three minutes later palmed out a Per Karlsson shot but it had already crossed the line.
A minute from the end Rangers' disastrous night was sealed when substitute Peter Eriksson latched onto a through pass, beat the stumbling defence and drove past a stranded Goram.
Goram stood little chance with any of the goals, blame for which could be laid squarely at the feet of the hapless back four, who appeared lethargic and uncommitted.
There were bookings for Rangers' pair Alex Cleland, for a trip on Robert Andersson, and England midfielder Paul Gascoigne, for a crude, lunging tackle.
Gascoigne, with only 45 minutes play behind him this season, only rarely showed any flashes of inspiration.

IFK Gothenburg: 1-Thomas Ravelli; 3-Magnus Johansson, 19-Magnus Erlingmark, 6-Teddy Lucic, 5-Olof Magnusson; 9-Niclas Alexandersson, 10-Stefan Pettersson, 11-Stefan Lindqvist, 28-Per Karlsson; 14-Andreas Andersson (8-Peter Eriksson, 87th) 20-Robert Andersson.

Rangers: 1-Andy Goram; 4-Sergio Porrini, 6-Joachim Bjorklund, 2-Alex Cleland, 17-Tony Vidmar; 8-Paul Gascoigne, 7-Jonas Thern, 3-Stale Stensas, 10-Jorg Albertz (12-Ian Ferguson, 69th); 9-Marco Negri (14-Ally McCoist, 69th) 15-Gordon Durie.
